author: Twillion
name: InGameCamera3D
description: Put a live picture on a screen inside your game: security monitors, television sets, rear-view mirrors, arcade cabinets and computer terminals. Add the "In-game camera" behavior to any 3D object and it films the layer it sits on from wherever you place it, so aiming a camera is just moving an object. You can also show a whole 3D layer through its own camera, or take a 2D layer straight onto a screen — a hidden 2D layer keeps running, so a minigame on an arcade cabinet is genuinely playable rather than a recording. Show any of them on a face of a 3D Box with the "Live screen" behavior. Also known as render to texture, or a render target.
shortDescription: Show a live camera, a 3D layer or a 2D layer on a screen inside your 3D game.

eventsBasedBehaviors.name: Camera3D
eventsBasedBehaviors.description: Turns this object into a camera. It films the 3D layer it sits on, from wherever you put it, and the result can be shown on any screen carrying the "Live screen" behavior. Aim it by moving and rotating the object — with a tween, a behavior, or by hand. The camera never appears in its own picture.

propertyDescriptors.name: Resolution
propertyDescriptors.label: Resolution
propertyDescriptors.description: Size of this camera’s texture. It sets the shape of the shot as well as the detail — SD is 4:3, HD is 16:9 — so changing it re-frames the picture. Lower costs less and gives a genuinely low-resolution image rather than a filter.

propertyDescriptors.name: Width
propertyDescriptors.label: Custom width
propertyDescriptors.description: Used only when Resolution is Custom.

propertyDescriptors.name: Height
propertyDescriptors.label: Custom height
propertyDescriptors.description: Used only when Resolution is Custom.

propertyDescriptors.name: Filtering
propertyDescriptors.label: Filtering
propertyDescriptors.description: Nearest keeps a crisp pixel grid at low resolutions. Linear smooths it. Low resolution with Nearest is the classic security-camera look.

propertyDescriptors.name: Near
propertyDescriptors.label: Near plane
propertyDescriptors.description: Anything closer to the camera than this is not filmed.

propertyDescriptors.name: Far
propertyDescriptors.label: Far plane
propertyDescriptors.description: Anything further from the camera than this is not filmed.

propertyDescriptors.name: FPSCap
propertyDescriptors.label: Frame rate cap
propertyDescriptors.description: How often this camera re-renders, in frames per second. 0 means every frame. Lowering it is the single biggest saving available, and 10 to 15 also gives an authentic surveillance judder.

propertyDescriptors.name: Enabled
propertyDescriptors.label: On
propertyDescriptors.description: When off, the camera stops rendering and its screens keep the last frame they were given — so a switched-off camera still looks like a working monitor.

propertyDescriptors.name: ShadowMode
propertyDescriptors.label: Shadows
propertyDescriptors.description: Reuse borrows the shadows already computed for the player’s view. It is much faster, and it is why this is the default, but shadows can look stale somewhere the player has never looked. PerPass recomputes them at full cost.

propertyDescriptors.name: Antialiasing
propertyDescriptors.label: Antialiasing samples
propertyDescriptors.description: Smooths jagged edges in the camera picture. 0 is off. Leave it off at low resolutions — it softens the very pixel grid those presets exist to show. Worth turning on only for HD screens the player gets close to.

propertyDescriptors.name: ForwardAxis
propertyDescriptors.label: Films along
propertyDescriptors.description: Which of this object’s own axes the camera looks down. +X means an angle of 0 faces right, the same as a 2D sprite. Change it if you put this behavior on a camera model that points a different way.

eventsBasedBehaviors.name: LiveScreen
eventsBasedBehaviors.description: Shows a live feed on a face of this 3D Box. The feed can come from an in-game camera, from a whole 3D layer, or straight from a 2D layer — useful for arcade cabinets and computer screens.

propertyDescriptors.name: MaterialMode
propertyDescriptors.label: Screen lighting
propertyDescriptors.description: Unlit keeps the screen at full brightness, like a real monitor. Lit lets the scene’s lighting dim it. Neither makes the screen light up the room — add a light for that.

propertyDescriptors.name: DoubleSided
propertyDescriptors.label: Visible from both sides
propertyDescriptors.description: Draw the screen from behind as well as in front.
